皇路"Mr. Minato! Still in that get-up? Home you have not gone?"
Kageaki"No. There is something I have to do."
皇路"...? Don't tell me you have come specially to congratulate us?"
皇路"Arre, forgive me, kept you waiting, did I? These reporters, one goes and another arrives. Haha, what to do—"
Kageaki"I regret to say, no."
皇路"...Hm?"
Kageaki"I truly regret it. That is not my business here, Mr. Oji."
皇路"...Then what, exactly?"
Kageaki"I have come to perform my duty as police. The duty of exposing a crime."
皇路"...!"
操"..."
Kageaki"Suguru Oji and Misao Oji, of Tamura Armor Works. I am arresting you both on suspicion of murder."
Kageaki"Come with me to the station."
皇路"...What is this? What nonsense? Please, I understand nothing."
皇路"Is it Ultima's accident? In armor racing such things are not even rare..."
Kageaki"Yes."
Kageaki"Ultima went into the spectator stands, exploded and burned. Six dead, the rider included. Fifteen injured."
操"...!"
Kageaki"And yes, in armor racing such a thing can happen. By itself it is nothing exceptional."
Kageaki"—if it was an accident・・."
皇路"It was! And we had nothing to do with it. Ultima's rider panicked and made an error, that is all!"
Kageaki"NoNo."
皇路"Ugh...!?"
Kageaki"Ultima had no reason to panic. In that situation, the ones who were panicking were none other than you."
Kageaki"Am I wrong?"
皇路"...Well, yes, we also felt the pressure. But so did Shokyo. The side that is ahead has its own tension, Mr. Minato."
Kageaki"I do not deny that. But I know something of Shokyo's rider. He is not a man to lose skill he has built up because of tension of that kind."
皇路"So what? So you say we must have done something!?"
皇路"What sort of twisted logic is this! One thing to another you are joining, Mr. Minato, with no connection at all! Defamation, this is!"
皇路"I should take you to court! But your favor I have not forgotten, so this once I will let it pass. Go home, please! Go!"
Kageaki"............"
皇路"...!"
Kageaki"At that moment, only a very few people could confirm it・・: myself, who was watching both machines from behind—"
Kageaki"—and a spectator who was extremely attentive, and whose seat and line of sight happened to be right. There cannot be many such people. But there was at least one."
